biomarkers.name: HER2
biomarkers.clinical_use: Guides treatment of underlying disease if invasive

biomarkers.name: ER
biomarkers.prevalence: Often negative in Paget cells despite ER+ in underlying tumour

biomarkers.name: CK7
biomarkers.prevalence: Positive in the vast majority of cases
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinguishes Paget cells from melanocytes / squamous cells

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Large clear Paget cells with abundant pale cytoplasm scattered within the nipple/areolar epidermis
variants: Paget disease with underlying invasive carcinoma
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Grade of underlying disease drives management

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Eczematoid clinical appearance often mistaken for dermatitis

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Usually ductal carcinoma cells (Paget cells) migrating within nipple epidermis; underlying source is most often invasive or in situ ductal carcinoma
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Retains ductal luminal/glandular differentiation (typically CK7+, often GCDFP-15+) with epidermal migration; distinct from primary epidermal disease
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Represents migratory behaviour of ductal carcinoma cells within the epidermis — not transdifferentiation to squamous phenotype (Paget cells remain glandular)
